checks: Verified source c58c06a13eeebb18:01, proposition and §§1–4 equations (1)–(11). The same measure and same constant (M+m_0)/(2(q+1)) are retained. The lexicographic rule is applied to the entire qualifying compact centerpoint set.

An equal point in each of the two reflected fibers has its midpoint in K_0, so K_0 is nonempty and contains all fibers. A finite union of the isometric copies of convex fibers has dimension equal to the largest fiber dimension, q=dim K_0. Their intrinsic measures add because the lifted fibers are disjoint.

For q≥1 the continuous Borel centerpoint theorem applies to the finite measure on the common q-dimensional affine space. Its positive-depth level excludes all points outside K_0 by strict separation. Closed through-cap upper semicontinuity, followed by compact lexicographic minimization, is valid even with mass on boundaries. The q=0 case selects the unique point.

For any through-cap the two traces on an identical pair have opposite offsets of the same continuous functional. One offset is nonpositive, so its trace contains the unshifted closed G, including the case G is the whole affine space. The central trace contributes mu_0(G) and the pair sum is precisely half of the marginal with the central contribution counted twice.

The sharp comparison after dividing by M is equivalent to 2^(n−1)(1+m_0/M)≥(q+1)Gamma_d. At q=d=2 the right side is 4/3, giving the two stated regimes. For the adjacent radius example with n=6 and a=1/3, the 728 nonzero lattice sites each have 1/9 of the central area, so m_0/M=9/737 and the bound is 373/2211.
